stand: Beijing's foreign ministry dismissed the Zhang spying case as 'hype' over so-called Chinese spies, its first response. The US State Department called China's maritime activity off Taiwan's east coast 'deeply destabilising', as Taipei says Beijing is rehearsing a blockade. Taiwanese and US authorities indicted 11 people for smuggling US chips to China for PLA use; a PLA researcher reportedly used Claude to simulate electronic-warfare attacks on Taiwanese radar and air bases. Former president Tsai Ing-wen began a US visit; analysts doubt Taiwan frictions will derail the Washington-Beijing reset.

figures.label: US troops in Keen Sword exercise

claims.text: FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, a California woman, for spying on Taiwan President Lai Ching-te's son's family for China.
claims.by: Says: FBI / US Justice Department. Denies: no response yet from China.

claims.text: Zhang travelled to Seattle at Chinese officials' direction and sent them photos, video and license-plate data on Lai's son's family.
claims.by: Says: US Justice Department. Denies: not addressed by China.

claims.text: Zhang's surveillance target was Lai Ting-yu, identified via a news report, not named directly by the FBI.
claims.by: Says: media report shared by FBI. Denies: FBI itself did not confirm the name.

claims.text: FBI Director Kash Patel says China sent an operative to surveil the Lai family on US soil.
claims.by: Says: FBI Director Kash Patel. Denies: no Chinese comment.

claims.text: Taiwan's presidential office calls the surveillance case transnational repression.
claims.by: Says: Taiwan presidential office spokesperson Karen Kuo. Denies: China has not commented.

claims.text: China has made no official response to the spying allegation.
claims.by: Says: n/a. Denies: Chinese embassy and foreign ministry gave no comment.

claims.text: Pentagon reportedly plans to station two defence officials inside Taiwan's defence ministry headquarters through 2028.
claims.by: Says: Taiwanese media reports. Denies: not confirmed by Pentagon or Taiwan's defence ministry.

claims.text: Taiwan's foreign minister Lin Chia-lung visited Phoenix for the opening of a new de facto Taiwan consulate, days after the Xi-Trump summit. Changed: purpose of the Arizona visit specified.
claims.by: Says: CNBC reporting. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Carter Centre survey finds mainland Chinese favour peaceful reunification but would back a military response to a formal independence declaration.
claims.by: Says: Carter Centre/Emory University China Pulse survey researcher Nick Zeller. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Beijing policy institutes are drafting proposals on how a reunified Taiwan would be governed, varying by how reunification occurs.
claims.by: Says: mainland Chinese scholars cited by SCMP. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Zhang charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent; prosecutors say she used tradecraft to avoid detection and never disclosed working for a foreign government.
claims.by: Says: US attorney Bill Essayli, Justice Department. Denies: not addressed by China.

claims.text: China's Taiwan Affairs Office called on Taiwan not to use dangerous or heavy-handed methods against mainland fishing vessels and crews.
claims.by: Says: Taiwan Affairs Office of the PRC State Council. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: North Korea's KCNA backed Beijing's One China policy and accused Washington of fuelling tension in the Taiwan Strait through arms sales to Taiwan.
claims.by: Says: KCNA commentary by analyst Kim Myong Chol. Denies: not addressed by US or Taiwan.

claims.text: A North Korean state media commentary claimed US arms sales to Taiwan over the past decade exceeded US$39 billion.
claims.by: Says: KCNA commentary by analyst Kim Myong-chol. Denies: not verified independently.

claims.text: US defence firm Aevex plans to manufacture combat-tested drones in Taiwan, designed to resist electronic warfare based on lessons from Ukraine.
claims.by: Says: Aevex executives, cited by SCMP. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: A mainland poll found opinion split on using force for reunification: 38% say it should never be used, 47% disagree.
claims.by: Says: unnamed poll cited by The Diplomat. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Same poll: if Taiwan declared independence, 81% of mainlanders would back limited operations on offshore islands, but only 32% a full-scale attack.
claims.by: Says: unnamed poll cited by The Diplomat. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: KCNA analyst says Taiwan's return to China is a matter of time and warns Washington against frontal confrontation with China over Taiwan.
claims.by: Says: KCNA commentary by analyst Kim Myong-chol. Denies: not addressed by US or Taiwan.

claims.text: A Taiwan-based war game run by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies found the US underprepared for a Chinese cyberattack and economic-pressure campaign against Taiwan that stops short of invasion.
claims.by: Says: FDD organisers Mark Montgomery and Craig Singleton.

claims.text: US intelligence assesses China has no fixed timeline to invade Taiwan and did not plan to do so in 2027.
claims.by: Says: Office of the Director of National Intelligence, 2026 worldwide threat assessment.

claims.text: US officials increasingly assess a Chinese invasion of Taiwan before 2028 as unlikely, citing military readiness delays and Taiwan's election calendar.
claims.by: Says: unnamed US officials, cited by Defense One.

claims.text: FDD's Mark Montgomery warns China could intensify cyber and economic coercion against Taiwan in early 2028 if the Democratic Progressive Party wins a fourth term.
claims.by: Says: FDD senior fellow Mark Montgomery.

claims.text: The Philippine Coast Guard commissioned a retired Taiwanese cutter, transferred quietly via a Philippine NGO rather than government-to-government, given Manila's One China policy.
claims.by: Says: We Protect Our Seas Foundation, cited by The Diplomat.

claims.text: A federal judge denied bail for Wanying Zhang, rejecting defence arguments that her surveillance of Lai's son's family was limited to a single day and did not show she was a flight risk.
claims.by: Says: US Magistrate Judge Steve Kim, siding with prosecutors. Denies: Zhang's lawyers argued the case covered only one day, 1 September 2025.

claims.text: A senior US diplomat says investors are overpricing the risk of conflict in the Taiwan Strait, citing deterrence as sufficient to prevent China acting by 2027.
claims.by: Says: US Assistant Secretary of State Michael DeSombre. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: The US has held back approval of a new $14 billion arms sale package to Taiwan, after an earlier $11 billion package drew a sharp response from Beijing in December.
claims.by: Says: CNBC, citing US government status. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: A Chinese military boat was spotted with two other vessels off Taiwan's Pacific coast in August, the first such sighting.
claims.by: Says: Reuters surveillance report, cited by CNBC. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Beijing has been courting Taiwan's opposition Kuomintang party since last year ahead of Taiwan's 2028 presidential election.
claims.by: Says: CNBC. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: This year's expanded Keen Sword exercise will deploy US and Japanese mobile missile systems to Yonaguni Island, with about 12,000 US troops reportedly taking part.
claims.by: Says: SCMP, citing unnamed reports. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines move from observer to participant status in this year's Keen Sword exercise, joined by Australia and Canada.
claims.by: Says: SCMP. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: Former US officials warn Washington's transactional approach puts the Indo-Pacific at risk, citing sharply increased US demands for Taiwan to boost burden-sharing and weapons production.
claims.by: Says: former US official Christensen, cited by SCMP. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: A former American commander says the US has not been in a weaker position in the western Pacific than it is now.
claims.by: Says: unnamed former US commander, cited by SCMP. Denies: not disputed.

claims.text: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs dismissed the Zhang spying case as hype over so-called 'Chinese spies', without addressing the specifics. Changed: Beijing has now responded.
claims.by: Says: FBI/Justice Department allege spying. Denies: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, calling it hype.

claims.text: The US State Department called China's maritime activity off Taiwan's east coast deeply destabilising, saying it undermines the peaceful resolution of the dispute.
claims.by: Says: US State Department spokesperson.

claims.text: Taiwanese officials believe China is practising for a possible maritime blockade of Taiwan's east coast, using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.
claims.by: Says: Taiwanese officials.

claims.text: Taiwan's Coast Guard says the Chinese militia boat and two accompanying vessels sighted off the east coast operated outside Taiwan's restricted waters.
claims.by: Says: Taiwan's Coast Guard.

claims.text: In June, Britain, France, Germany and the US jointly expressed concern over Chinese activity off Taiwan's east coast as a threat to regional stability.
claims.by: Says: Britain, France, Germany and the US.

claims.text: Taiwanese prosecutors charged 10 people on 6 October with reselling export-controlled semiconductor chips to China from 2017, forging documents claiming to represent Taiwan's defence research institute NCSIST.
claims.by: Says: Taiwanese prosecutors.

claims.text: Taiwanese authorities say the PLA sought the smuggled chips for use in missiles and radar systems.
claims.by: Says: Taiwanese authorities.

claims.text: US authorities arrested California resident Greg Lui on 1 October for reselling about $300 million of export-controlled Nvidia chips to China via Singapore and Malaysia.
claims.by: Says: US authorities.

claims.text: A PLA-affiliated researcher reportedly used Claude to build software simulating coordinated electronic-warfare attacks on Taiwanese radar installations and air bases, between December 2025 and August 2026.
claims.by: Says: ISW report.

claims.text: Taiwan's former president Tsai Ing-wen began a weeklong US visit the same day foreign minister Lin Chia-lung attended the opening of a Phoenix de facto consulate.
claims.by: Says: SCMP, citing diplomatic observers.

claims.text: Diplomatic analysts say recent Taiwan-related events are unlikely to derail the Washington-Beijing reset, though the fate of the $14bn arms package remains a key concern.
claims.by: Says: diplomatic analysts, cited by SCMP.

claims.text: China's Taiwan Affairs Office said writers on both sides should uphold a 'national standpoint' after Taiwanese author Yang Shuang-zi won the 2026 International Booker Prize.
claims.by: Says: China's Taiwan Affairs Office.

claims.text: The World Coffee Championships website dropped references to Taiwan for 2026 champion Lin Shao-hsing, now listing her as representing 'Chinese Taipei'.
claims.by: Says: DW report, citing the World Coffee Championships website.

claims.text: A 2026 National Chengchi University poll found the vast majority of Taiwanese identify as 'Taiwanese', with only 2.5% identifying as Chinese.
claims.by: Says: National Chengchi University Election Study Center poll.

timeline.text: Xi-Trump summit; China presses US to harden Taiwan line.
Taiwan Coast Guard detains a Chinese fishing vessel near Penghu, holding its seven crew members.
Okinawa Defense Bureau relays Yonaguni NMESIS/MADIS deployment plans.
A Chinese fishing vessel clashes with Taiwan's Coast Guard near the Pratas Islands; the Coast Guard uses a water cannon to force it away.
US authorities arrest Greg Lui in California for reselling export-controlled Nvidia chips to China via Singapore and Malaysia.
Yonaguni's local government discloses the NMESIS/MADIS deployment.
Philippine Coast Guard commissions BRP Sarangani, a retired Taiwanese cutter acquired via an NGO intermediary.
Taiwan's foreign minister Lin Chia-lung arrives in Phoenix for a three-day visit.
Lin's Phoenix visit is for the opening of a new de facto Taiwan consulate.
FBI arrests Wanying Zhang at LAX before a flight to China.
Taiwan's presidential office calls the case a classic case of transnational repression.
Taiwanese media report the unconfirmed Pentagon plan to post officials in Taiwan's defence ministry.
Zhang due in Los Angeles federal court.
Tsai Ing-wen begins a weeklong US visit as Lin Chia-lung attends the Phoenix consulate opening.
Taiwanese prosecutors charge 10 people with reselling export-controlled chips to China since 2017.
China's foreign ministry dismisses the Zhang spying case as hype over so-called 'Chinese spies'.
North Korea's KCNA backs China's One China policy and warns Washington over Taiwan arms sales.
Defense One reports FDD war-game findings on US cyberdefense gaps over Taiwan.
A US judge denies bail for Wanying Zhang, citing her family's ties in China.
SCMP reports an expanded Keen Sword exercise will deploy mobile missile systems to Yonaguni, with new participant nations.
Ex-US officials warn Washington's transactional Taiwan policy risks destabilising the Indo-Pacific.
A senior US diplomat says investors are overpricing the risk of conflict in the Taiwan Strait.
US State Department calls China's maritime activity off Taiwan's east coast deeply destabilising.
NMESIS and MADIS systems first arrive with Okinawa-based Marine unit.
Zhang travels to Seattle at Chinese officials' direction and surveils Lai's son's family.
FDD runs a Taiwan-based cyber war game simulating Chinese disruption of communications and infrastructure short of invasion.
A Chinese military boat is sighted off Taiwan's Pacific coast for the first time.
Taiwanese barista Lin Shao-hsing wins the World Latte Art Championship; the event's website later drops references to Taiwan.
Britain, France, Germany and the US jointly express concern over Chinese activity off Taiwan's east coast.

headline: China dismisses Taiwan spy case as Washington brands its maritime pressure destabilising
